notes: A. James Clark School of Engineering official Fall 2026 Fire Protection Engineering graduation plan. General-education slots (ENGL101, Oral Communication, Professional Writing, Scholarship in Practice, Humanities, History/Social Sciences, Big Question, Understanding Plural Societies/Cultural Competency) are left out: only the program's own requirements are audited here (they're covered by gen-ed-2026-27.ts).

The 'MATH 240 or 241' slot (Year 2 Fall) is filled with MATH241 (Calculus III), as printed first on the graduation plan's own overview page; MATH240 would satisfy the requirement equally, but MATH241 avoids a real-world credit conflict with the MATH461 technical elective below (per the course catalog, credit is only granted for one of MATH240, MATH341 or MATH461).

The four generic 'Technical Elective**' slots (Year 3 Fall/Spring, Year 4 Fall/Spring) are filled with MATH461 (Linear Algebra for Scientists and Engineers, satisfying the 3-credit MATH400+/STAT400+ bucket), ENFP464 (satisfying the 3-credit ENFP400+ bucket, distinct from the 9 ENFP courses already required), and CHEM425 plus CHEM474 (satisfying the 6-credit CHEM/CMSC/MATH/PHYS 400+ bucket). These four are real UMD courses already cited as approved technical electives for a neighboring ENGR major in this repo (chbe-major-2026-27.ts); no source for this major names specific technical-elective course numbers, so any courses satisfying the three buckets in fpe-major-2026-27.ts would equally work -- see its reviewNotes.
